在樂器分類中，框式箏指弦張於開放框架而無內建共鳴器的弦鳴樂器。其較明確的發展與傳: In instrument classification, the frame zither means a chordophone whose strings are stretched on an open frame with no built-in resonator. Its clearer development and spread are found in Africa: the Kru of Liberia have a triangular frame zither, also found in Sierra Leone and Guinea; Nuba women in Sudan bend a stick into a round frame, wind a single string several turns around it, and set it on a gourd to resonate. Medieval European illustrations show similar shapes, but they are unclear, so it is hard to tell whether they are frame zithers, harps or lyres.

框式箏屬箏類下的簡單弦鳴樂器，霍恩博斯特尔—薩克斯編號316，以開放框架張弦，可: The frame zither is a simple chordophone within the zither class, Hornbostel–Sachs number 316, with strings stretched on an open frame and a gourd or clay pot added for resonance. In playing, the opening of the resonator is often held against the chest or belly, or the round frame is set on a gourd. In Africa triangular or round frames are common; the Kru of Liberia use them, and they are found in Sierra Leone and Guinea as well; Nuba women in Sudan wind a single string into three or four segments.
框式箏的弦張於開放框上，本身不一定有內建共鳴箱；演奏者可附加葫蘆或陶罐共鳴。非洲: The strings of the frame zither are stretched on an open frame, which need not have a built-in soundbox; the player may add a gourd or clay pot for resonance. In the African triangular type the opening of the resonator is held against the chest or belly, and the round frame is set on a gourd, so that the vibration of the strings is amplified through the resonator. Unlike the harp, whose strings run to a soundboard set into the end of the frame, and unlike the psaltery, which has a parallel board behind the strings as a soundbox, the frame zither has neither. The source records neither the range nor how volume is controlled.
框式箏的琴身以木製框架為主，非洲三角形形式用三根木臂構成，圓形形式則將木棍彎成圓: The body of the frame zither is mainly a wooden frame; the African triangular form is built from three wooden arms, and the round form bends a stick into a hoop. The resonator is usually a cut gourd, or the instrument is set on a gourd; the source also mentions a clay pot attached or placed inside as a resonator. The sounding body is the string stretched across the frame, but the material of the string is not stated. Beyond wood, gourd and clay pot, the source gives no materials for the other parts.
演奏時可將共鳴器開口貼在胸部或腹部，使樂器保持在手臂可及範圍內。圓形框式箏則置於: In playing, the opening of the resonator can be held against the chest or belly, keeping the instrument within reach of the arms. The round frame zither is set on a gourd, which provides the resonance. The basic order of operations is: stretch the strings on the three arms or the round frame, use a gourd or clay pot as a resonator where needed, and then hold and play the instrument as described above.
